questions.prompt: Which pope, elected in 1978, was the first non-Italian pope in more than 450 years?
questions.explanation: Karol Wojtyla of Poland was elected on 16 October 1978 as John Paul II, the first non-Italian pope since Adrian VI in the 1520s and the first from a Slavic country.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - St. John Paul II

questions.prompt: Which spacecraft carried the first crew of more than one person into Earth orbit, in 1964?
questions.explanation: Voskhod 1 carried three Soviet cosmonauts into orbit on 12 October 1964: a commander, an engineer, and a doctor, the first physician in space.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Voskhod

questions.prompt: Which Dutch navigator skirted the southern shores of the island later named Tasmania in 1642?
questions.explanation: Sailing from Batavia (Jakarta) to test a sea passage eastward to Chile and to explore New Guinea, Abel Janszoon Tasman skirted the southern shores of Tasmania on 24 November 1642.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 24

questions.prompt: Canada's 1929 Persons Case opened the way for women to be appointed to which institution?
questions.explanation: On 18 October 1929 the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council overruled Canada's Supreme Court, opening the door for women to be appointed to the Senate. The case was brought by five Alberta women known as the Famous Five.

sources.displayName: Senate of Canada - Why the Persons Case Matters

questions.prompt: Who proclaimed Bulgaria's full independence from the Ottoman Empire in 1908 and took the title of tsar?
questions.explanation: On 5 October 1908 Ferdinand, prince of Bulgaria since 1887, proclaimed the country's full independence from the Ottoman Empire and assumed the title of king, or tsar.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Ferdinand (king of Bulgaria)

questions.prompt: At his coronation as emperor of France in 1804, who crowned Napoleon?
questions.explanation: On 2 December 1804 Napoleon crowned himself emperor of France, with Pope Pius VII present at the ceremony.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 2

questions.prompt: About how long were the 33 miners trapped in Chile's San Jose mine before their rescue in October 2010?
questions.explanation: The 33 workers were rescued on 13 October 2010, 69 days after the mine collapsed on 5 August. For the first 17 days they had no contact with the surface.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Chile mine rescue of 2010

questions.prompt: Which space telescope, built as the successor to Hubble, launched on 25 December 2021?
questions.explanation: The James Webb Space Telescope, designed and built by U.S., Canadian, and European space agencies as Hubble's successor, launched on Christmas Day 2021.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

questions.prompt: A 1275 toll privilege from the Count of Holland is the first document to name which city?
questions.explanation: Drawn up in Leiden on 27 October 1275, Count Floris V's toll privilege spared people living near the dam on the Amstel from his tolls; it is the first document to name Amsterdam, which marks the date as its birthday.

questions.prompt: Who led the Haitian forces that defeated the French at the Battle of Vertieres in 1803?
questions.explanation: Haitian forces led by Jean-Jacques Dessalines defeated the French at Vertieres on 18 November 1803, effectively ending the Haitian Revolution weeks before Haiti declared independence.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 18

questions.prompt: Whose 1910 revolt, though it failed, sparked the Mexican Revolution?
questions.explanation: Francisco Madero launched a failed revolt on 20 November 1910 that sparked the Mexican Revolution, inspiring leaders such as Pancho Villa and Emiliano Zapata to mobilize against President Porfirio Diaz.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 20

questions.prompt: What did Mexico's Ley Juarez of 1855 abolish?

options.text: Special courts for the clergy and military

questions.explanation: Passed on 23 November 1855, the Ley Juarez abolished special courts for the clergy and military, part of justice minister Benito Juarez's effort to remove remnants of colonialism and promote equality.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 23

questions.prompt: Which gym teacher organized the first game of basketball in 1891?
questions.explanation: James Naismith organized the first basketball game on 21 December 1891 at a school in Springfield, Massachusetts. It was so chaotic that he went on to write the sport's original rules.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

questions.prompt: The 1820 sinking of which whaling ship, rammed by a sperm whale, inspired the climax of Moby-Dick?
questions.explanation: On 20 November 1820 the American whaleship Essex was rammed by a sperm whale and later sank, inspiring the climactic scene of Herman Melville's Moby-Dick (1851).

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: November 20

questions.prompt: The Pact of Locarno, signed in 1925, was meant to guarantee peace in which region?
questions.explanation: On 1 December 1925 Germany, France, Belgium, Great Britain, and Italy signed the Pact of Locarno, a series of agreements intended to guarantee peace in western Europe.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 1

questions.prompt: What did the Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921 establish?

options.text: A Home Rule parliament in Dublin

questions.explanation: Signed on 6 December 1921 by British representatives and Irish leaders including Arthur Griffith and Michael Collins, the treaty ended the Irish War of Independence and established the Irish Free State.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 6

questions.prompt: Which country declared itself independent of Russia on 6 December 1917, following the Bolshevik Revolution?
questions.explanation: Finland declared its independence from Russia on 6 December 1917, weeks after the Bolshevik Revolution.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 6

questions.prompt: Which surgeon performed the first human heart transplant, in Cape Town in 1967?
questions.explanation: South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the first human heart transplant on 3 December 1967 at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 3

questions.prompt: The Great Chicago Fire of 1871 burned for about a week.
questions.explanation: The fire began on 8 October 1871 and burned until early on 10 October, about two days, devastating a wide swath of the city.

questions.prompt: Roald Amundsen's expedition was the first to reach the South Pole.
questions.explanation: Traveling with four companions, 52 dogs, and four sledges, Roald Amundsen became the first explorer to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911.

sources.displayName: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 14

questions.prompt: The Suez Canal opened in 1869 after about ten years of construction.
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal opened in Egypt on 17 November 1869, after ten years of construction.

questions.prompt: The 1943 Tehran Conference brought together Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin.
questions.explanation: The Tehran Conference opened on 28 November 1943 with U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin; Stalin pressed for an invasion of France.
